description:
Returns the address the invoice emails of the company are sent from and the defaults that
apply when an invoice is sent by email. It applies only to invoice emails.

- **`sender.source`, `sender.email_domain_id` and `sender.local_part`:** what the company
  chose. A `local_part` that is `null` means `facturas`.
- **`sender.effective`:** the address the next invoice email will go out from, and why
  (`reason`). With `source` `BEEL` it is the address of BeeL. Otherwise it is resolved in
  this order: the email domain chosen by the company and the default email domain of the
  account, then the address of BeeL. Only email domains that are verified, and only while
  the account holds the custom email domain add-on, count. The add-on is contracted with
  BeeL. `email_domain_id` is present only when the address uses one of the account's email
  domains.
- **`defaults`:** the content applied to an invoice email that does not specify its own. Each
  property is `null` when it is not set.
- **Domain no longer verified:** invoice emails go out from BeeL. without interruption, and
  `reason` reports it.
- **Environment:** the configuration belongs to the company and is the same in test and live.

BeeL API endpoint: GET /v1/companies/{company_id}/email-configuration (reference: https://docs.beel.es)

company_id.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the company the operation acts on: its identifier, not its NIF. It is the only source of context: the account that owns it is derived from it, and the `BeeL-Active-Company` header plays no part. A company you do not reach answers `403`, and so does a company that does not exist, so the existence of a company in another account is never disclosed.

name: beel_get_email_configuration
